setlist.title: Jerry Garcia commentary with Acid Test audio

liner.body_md:
## Setlist highlights

- **Jerry Garcia commentary with Acid Test audio**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [14]
- **Jerry Garcia Interview - Part A**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Jerry Garcia Interview - Part B**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Jerry Garcia Interview - Part C**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1967-XX-XX.sbd.bershaw.5419.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 4 songs; 68 min; rated 4.46/5 by 13 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the soundboard transfer sounds excellent [2]

## Around the show

- Garcia interview split into three parts, about an hour long, covering music, drugs, politics and social change around 1967 [1]
- Garcia muses in the interview about what being a wealthy musician would be like [3]
- After Garcia died, fans left flowers, candles, bears and photos on the house steps; a low gate was later added [4]
- Interview has Garcia discussing music, the San Francisco scene and other bands, from before the Dead left San Francisco [4]
- Asked why he smokes pot so often, Garcia answers simply that it feels good [7]
- Garcia comes across as an uneasy figurehead who leads by example rather than pushing beliefs on others [8]
- Reviewer says the house is at 710 Ashbury, not Haight, about a block and a half up from Haight Street [9]
- Interviewers were Randy Groeke and Mike Cramer; Groeke had been Garcia's banjo student in the early 1960s near Palo Alto [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1967-XX-XX.sbd.bershaw.5419.shnf**: transferred by Alan Bershaw; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Taken from the chronological Acid Test recordings compilation listed in The Grateful Dead Tapers Compendium Volume One [1]
